frame: Provisional frame: x forward, y to port, z up, metres. Origin x=0 at the stem (forward end of LOA, which is also the forestay deck point since SFJ=0), so points aft of the stem have negative x. y=0 on the centreline. z=0 on the ORC measurement-trim flotation plane (no crew, no sails), the plane the certificate freeboards are measured from. hull_hydro.json transform maps it to the body frame (origin at DWL midship): p_body = p + (stem_x_in_body, 0, flotation_z_in_body).

displacement_basis.value: The certificate displacement (1438 kg) is measured in IMS Measurement Trim: dry, light ship, without crew (IMS B4.1), and with sails, sheets and running rigging removed (B4.2(c),(d)). It includes battery and the outboard as carried (B4.1(b),(e)). So it is compared with the sum of in_displacement items with no crew term.
displacement_basis.source: IMS Rule 2020, B4 Measurement Trim; ORC J/80 OD certificate 2019, p.1

displacement.note: J/Boats publishes 1315 kg (2,900 lb). The certificate value is used: it is measured, and agrees with the class builder's weight range.

builders_weight_min.note: Hull, keel, rudder, deck, mouldings, fixed fittings, spars, standing and running rigging. Excludes battery, sails, cushions, portable equipment.

complete_boat_min.note: Builder's weight plus battery, outboard and mandatory equipment; correctors added if light.

items_basis.value: Each item has a cg (provisional frame) and, where its size is known, a shape: box (solid, uniform) or shell_box (thin uniform shell over all six faces), with dims [x, y, z] extents in metres, centred on the cg. Items without a shape are point masses. The item marked residual takes the certificate displacement minus the other in_displacement items, and its cg x is solved so the measurement-trim LCG equals the total LCB (hull_hydro.json result lcb_x_total) and its cg z so the measurement-trim VCG equals the certificate VCGM; sailcore's loader (core/src/boat_data.cpp) does both, and the values stored here record its result.
items_basis.source: IMS Rule 2020, B4 Measurement Trim; ORC J/80 OD certificate 2019, p.1

hull_deck_fittings.source: J/80 Class Rules 2024 D.5.1; ORC J/80 OD certificate 2019 (displacement, VCGM)
hull_deck_fittings.method: residual of 1438 kg; x solved so total LCG = total LCB, height solved so total VCG = certificate VCGM
hull_deck_fittings.note: 1438 kg minus the other in_displacement items (729.2 kg). Includes the GRP keel sump mass.

cg.source: DSYHS model 61, data/dsyhs/table.csv; ORC J/80 OD certificate 2019, p.1
cg.method: x and z both solved. x makes the total measurement-trim LCG equal the total LCB of the floating meshes (canoe, keel, fairing, rudder; hull_hydro.json result lcb_x_total, -0.3436 m in the body frame), so the boat floats level at the DWL; the loader rejects an x more than 0.5 m from the canoe-body LCB (result lcb_x_canoe). z makes the total measurement-trim VCG equal VCGM -0.076 m, i.e. 0.076 m below the flotation plane in ORC's z-up convention.

cg_z_bounds.method: plausible band above the flotation plane for hull, deck and fittings, between the canoe-body bottom region and above the sheer; the loader rejects a solved height outside it.

shape.source: J/Boats J/80 Tech Specs page (LWL); ORC J/80 OD certificate 2019, p.1 (beam)
shape.method: LWL x maximum beam x depth; depth is the canoe-body draft 0.2417 m (hull_hydro.json result tc) plus the sheer at the LCB station, 0.701 m (hull_hydro.json sheer fit).

keel_ballast.note: J/Boats: 1,400 lb lead-antimony keel. The H.1 offsets volume (0.0805 m^3) is the keel's displaced volume; its shape includes the GRP sump above the lead, so it is larger than the lead volume.

cg.source: J/80 Class Rules 2024 (effective 2024-06-01), Appendix H.1 Appendage Plan
cg.method: appendages.json keel ballast_centroid: centroid of the lead from the lead top depth to the tip; x inherits the root_leading_edge estimate.

shape.source: J/80 Class Rules 2024 (effective 2024-06-01), Appendix H.1 Appendage Plan
shape.method: box with the same second moments as the lead: NACA 4-digit sections of the H.1 offsets from the lead top depth (0.363 m below Section 1) to the elliptical tip, integrated for the variance of x, y and z about the lead centroid; each extent is sqrt(12 variance).

rudder.note: class minimum, including gudgeons and tiller; actual may be higher

cg.source: J/80 Class Rules 2024 (effective 2024-06-01), Appendix H.1 Appendage Plan
cg.method: blade about 19 kg at its volume centroid (0.521 m below the root, 0.42 chord aft of the stock axis, appendages.json rudder stock_axis) and tiller and gudgeons about 3 kg near the transom at the sheer (x -7.6, z +0.65).

shape.source: J/80 Class Rules 2024 (effective 2024-06-01), Appendix H.1 Appendage Plan
shape.method: blade mean chord, thickness and span (Sections 1-5).

mast.source: ORC J/80 OD certificate 2019, p.2; J/80 Class Rules 2024 (effective 2024-06-01), C.8.1
mast.note: MWT; class minimum. IMS F8.1(a) weighs the mast with its standing rigging, so wire, terminals and turnbuckles are in this figure.

cg.source: ORC J/80 OD certificate 2019, p.2; IMS Rule 2020, F8.2
cg.method: x on the mast axis at the sheer (rig.json mast_axis_at_sheer). z = mast heel + MCG 3.21 m, since IMS F8.2 measures MCG from the mast's lower point, not the sheer. The mast is keel-stepped (rig.json rig_type) and no source gives the step height, so the heel is taken at the canoe-body bottom on the centreline at the mast station, -0.228 m (hull_physics.obj section at body x 0.825 m).

shape.method: MDL1 x MDT1 x heel-to-top length (rig.json mast_top_above_water 11.35 m plus the 0.228 m heel depth), centred on the measured CG rather than on the mid-length. A uniform spar over the full length somewhat overstates its own pitch and roll inertia.

cg.method: mid-length of E aft of the mast aft face (x = -(J + MDL1) - E/2), at the boom band height less half BD (rig.json boom_height_above_water 2.044 m - 0.047 m); boom on the centreline.

shape.method: E x assumed width 0.06 m x BD.

jib_furler.source: J/80 Standard Building Specifications (1-Dec-20), items 59-69; IMS Rule 2020, F8.1(a)
jib_furler.method: furler drum and foil only. IMS F8.1(a) weighs the mast with its standing rigging, so the wire (about 6 kg from rig geometry) and about 1 kg of turnbuckles and toggles are already in MWT and are not a separate item; the furler is about 4 kg.

cg.method: foil about 3 kg at the forestay mid-point (rig.json forestay_deck_point to hounds_forestay_on_mast) and drum about 1 kg just above the forestay deck point.

battery.method: midpoint of the class range, 2 to 25 kg

cg.method: low in the hull under the forward cockpit, on the centreline; no source gives the battery location.

outboard_engine.method: class minimum (empty of fuel); the engine is carried while racing, so IMS B4.1(e) includes it.

cg.method: stowed below on the cabin sole aft of the mast, on the centreline; no source gives the stowage.

running_rigging.source: J/80 Standard Building Specifications (1-Dec-20), items 70-78; IMS Rule 2020, B4 Measurement Trim
running_rigging.method: sheets, halyards and control lines; in builder's weight but excluded from measurement trim by IMS B4.2(d).

cg.method: spread over the rig, so placed at the mast CG (see mast cg); tools/vpp/run_pyvpp.py uses the same height.
centroid of the sails.json main tack, head and clew; sail on the centreline.
centroid of the sails.json jib tack, head and clew; sail on the centreline.

keel_sump_volume.source: J/80 Class Rules 2024 (effective 2024-06-01), Appendix H.1 Appendage Plan

bulb_mass.source: J/80 Class Rules 2024 (effective 2024-06-01), Appendix H.1 Appendage Plan; J/Boats J/80 Tech Specs page
bulb_mass.method: offsets volume below Section 4 (0.0292 m^3) x 11 000 kg/m^3, assuming the lead fills from the tip up.

ballast_ratio.source: J/Boats J/80 Tech Specs page; ORC J/80 OD certificate 2019, p.1
ballast_ratio.method: keel_ballast / certificate displacement (1438 kg), which hydrostatics use.
ballast_ratio.note: J/Boats' 48% is 635/1315, using its lighter displacement figure.

crew_weight_max_class.note: in swimming apparel, any number of crew. The 2006 rules (C.3.1) had 338.6 kg or three people of any weight. The crew mass of the sailing configuration.

crew_weight_default_orc.note: ORC default; exceeds the class maximum. The crew mass of the ORC stability configuration.

orc_stability_gear.note: gear ORC adds to the default crew for the stability (LPS) calculation; combined with crew_weight_default_orc into one point mass.

orc_stability_crew_gear_z.note: height above the flotation plane of the combined crew and gear point mass, on the centreline. Its x is crew_cg_x.

crew_count.method: the class sets no crew number; 4 crew at about 87 kg reach the 350 kg cap, and 4 to 5 is usual.

crew_cg_x.method: mid-cockpit on the deck plan, where the crew sit hiking; no source gives a crew position. Provisional frame (stem origin).
crew_cg_x.note: the crew point mass's x in the sailing and ORC stability configurations; tools/vpp/run_pyvpp.py uses it for the crew VCG only, and the VPP takes the crew righting arm from ORC eq. 4.30

crew_cg_above_sheer.method: seated hip-to-chest height above the sheer for crew sitting on the deck edge; no source gives a crew height.
crew_cg_above_sheer.note: the default crew height in the sailing configuration, above the hull_hydro.json sheer fit at crew_cg_x.

added_mass.source: Fossen, Handbook of Marine Craft Hydrodynamics and Motion Control (2011); Newman, Marine Hydrodynamics (1977)
added_mass.method: surge added mass is surge_fraction of the rigid-body mass. Sway, heave and the rotations come from strip theory in the high-frequency (rigid free surface) limit: every section is a half-ellipse of half-beam BWL/2 and draft Tc (hull_hydro.json result), whose added mass is half the double-body ellipse's: sway rho pi Tc^2 / 2, heave rho pi (BWL/2)^2 / 2, roll about the waterline centre rho pi ((BWL/2)^2 - Tc^2)^2 / 16, per metre. Sections are integrated over an equivalent prism of length Cp x LWL, the length over which a uniform section holds the hull's volume; pitch and yaw use that prism's (Cp LWL)^2 / 12. The keel and rudder are not included. Each scale multiplies its strip value; an optional length_factor replaces Cp.
